dbe_source.recommendation: The period of a trig graph is a single number (e.g. 180), not an interval. The domain is the interval of x-values. Do not confuse the two.

lesson.concept: The period of a trig graph is a single number (e.g. 180), not an interval. The domain is the interval of x-values. Do not confuse the two.
lesson.why: This is one of the most frequent errors DBE reported for this section.

example.problem: State the period of y = sin x
work: Not x in [0; 360]. That is the domain.
The period is a single value.

probe.problem: State the period of y = cos x.

learner_message: The period is a single number. What you gave is an interval or an endpoint of the domain.
